draft.text: You came in because you have swelling and pain in your wrist after hitting a pole while playing tennis.
You have tenderness near your wrist, especially when pressing on the area.
The pain gets worse when you move your wrist or bend your thumb.
You likely have a wrist injury from the recent trauma.
You do not have numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hand or fingers.
The doctor will look at the X-ray results.
You will need to come back in one week for a follow-up.
You should apply ice and take over-the-counter pain medicine as needed.
Avoid heavy lifting or bending to prevent making the injury worse.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have had wrist pain and swelling for two weeks after hitting a pole while playing tennis.
You have tenderness near your wrist, especially when pressing on the area.
The pain gets worse when you move your wrist or bend your thumb.
It seems like you have a wrist injury from the recent trauma.
There is no numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hand or fingers.
The doctor will look at the X-ray results, which were normal.
You will need to come back in one week for a follow-up.
You should apply ice to the area and take over-the-counter pain medicine if needed.
Avoid heavy lifting or bending and adjust your activities to prevent making the injury worse.
